cohort: The study included 336 women of reproductive age, with gestational amenorrhea >30 weeks, who had one or two previous cesarean sections and were undergoing an emergency or elective cesarean section.
finding: Women with a history of recurrent cesarean sections experience several intraoperative morbidities, with dense intraoperative adhesions, extremely thinned out lower uterine segment, and scar dehiscence occurring at different rates depending on the number of previous C-sections.
mod_finding: Women with two previous caesarean sections experienced significantly higher rates of dense intraoperative adhesions (77.6%) compared to those with one previous caesarean section (23.7%), with differing rates also observed for extremely thinned out lower uterine segment and scar dehiscence.
